lessons.title: 话题、内容与特征关系
examples: A lecture on climate change begins now.
The girl with glasses is Amy.

exampleNotes.body: 一般话题用 about。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: on climate change 后置修饰 lecture，中文通常前移为“关于气候变化的讲座”。
exampleNotes.detail: 正式主题可用 on。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: with glasses 后置修饰 girl，中文前移为“戴眼镜的女孩”。
exampleNotes.detail: 表示具有某特征用 with。

rules: about 表示一般谈论的话题；on 常用于更正式或专业的主题。
on 可表示书籍、讲座、文章等正式内容的主题。
of 常表示所属、组成或内容；with 常表示具有某物或某特征。

questions.question: 我们聊了旅行：talked ___ the trip
questions.correct: 一般话题用 about。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：一般话题用 about。

questions.question: 一场关于科学的讲座：a lecture ___ science
questions.correct: 正式主题可用 on。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：正式主题可用 on。

questions.question: 戴眼镜的女孩：the girl ___ glasses
questions.correct: 表示具有某特征用 with。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：表示具有某特征用 with。

narration.text: 谈话围绕旅行、讲座聚焦气候变化、女孩带着眼镜，这三句都在名词或动作旁补信息，却建立不同关系。<#0.4#>We talked about the trip。<#0.8#>about the trip 说明谈话围绕什么话题，修补的是 talked 的内容范围。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>A lecture on climate change begins now。<#0.8#>on climate change 紧跟 lecture，告诉我们讲座的专题，语气通常比普通谈话的 about 更聚焦、正式。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The girl with glasses is Amy。<#0.8#>with glasses 不是谈话内容，而是给 girl 增加外在特征，帮助听者认出是哪位女孩。<#0.8#>判断时先问短语靠着谁、在补什么：围绕动作的谈论内容常用 about；讲座、文章等聚焦的专题可用 on；给人物或事物附加“带有什么”的特征，用 with。不要因为中文都能出现“关于、有”就混选。

lessons.title: 介词短语作补足成分
lessons.meta: 补足动词 · 形容词 · 名词意义
examples: She is proud of her work.
The need for change is clear.

exampleNotes.body: depend 与 on 搭配并由其补足意义。
proud 后用 of。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: for change 补足 need 的内容，中文译为“改变的需要”。
exampleNotes.detail: reason 表示原因时常接 for。

rules: 有些动词需要特定介词短语补足意义，如 depend on。
形容词也可选择特定介词短语，如 proud of。
名词可由介词短语补足具体内容，如 need for、reason for。

questions.question: Success depends ___ effort.
questions.correct: depend 与 on 搭配并由其补足意义。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：depend 与 on 搭配并由其补足意义。

questions.question: She is proud ___ her work.
questions.correct: proud 后用 of。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：proud 后用 of。

questions.question: the reason ___ the delay
questions.correct: reason 表示原因时常接 for。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：reason 表示原因时常接 for。

narration.text: 有些词说到一半，会让人自然追问“依靠什么、为哪件事骄傲、对什么的需要”。介词短语负责把这种未完成的关系补齐。<#0.4#>Success depends on effort。<#0.8#>depends 会追问依靠什么，on effort 是动词需要的补足成分。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She is proud of her work。<#0.8#>proud 只说“骄傲”还没有交代对象，of her work 补清骄傲所针对的事情，所以补足形容词 proud。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The need for change is clear。<#0.8#>for change 紧跟名词 need，说明是什么方面的需要，补足名词意义。<#0.8#>本节与普通状语不同：状语多是可选背景，补足成分由前面的中心词强烈要求。判断时先找介词短语前的动词、形容词或名词，再问去掉短语后是否留下“对谁、关于什么、依靠什么”的明显空缺；有空缺，就按相应中心词的补足成分分析。

lessons.title: 介词改变关系意义
lessons.meta: 同一中心词后的关系变化

analyses.label: 介词补足语：就事项达成一致

exampleNotes.body: 同意某人用 agree with。
就日期达成一致用 agree on。
接受提议用 agree to。

rules: agree with 后接人或观点，表示赞同。
agree on 后接议题或安排，表示就某事达成一致。
agree to 后接计划、条件或提议，表示接受。

questions.question: agree ___ you
questions.correct: 同意某人用 agree with。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：同意某人用 agree with。

questions.question: agree ___ the date
questions.correct: 就日期达成一致用 agree on。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：就日期达成一致用 agree on。

questions.question: agree ___ the proposal
questions.correct: 接受提议用 agree to。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：接受提议用 agree to。

narration.text: 同一个 agree，后面的介词一换，谈的对象类型也会变化。<#0.4#>I agree with you。<#0.8#>with 把我和 you 放进同一意见关系，表示我赞同你这个人表达的看法。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>We agreed on the date。<#0.8#>on the date 把 date 当成双方讨论后共同确定的事项，重点是就日期达成一致。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>They agreed to the plan。<#0.8#>to the plan 表示他们把同意指向这个方案，接受方案本身。<#0.8#>本节不是再背三个搭配，而是观察介词怎样改变 agree 后的关系：with 常连意见一致的人，on 常连协商确定的事项，to 常连被接受的建议或方案。判断时先辨认后面是人、共同议定事项，还是需要接受的内容；再选介词，并把整个关系放回语境检查。

lessons.title: 复杂介词宾语与介词后置
lessons.meta: wh-从句 · 疑问句 · 定语从句
examples: We talked about what he said.
The person I spoke to is here.

analyses.label: 省略关系词的定语从句

exampleNotes.body: 介词后用陈述语序的 wh-从句。
日常表达常把介词 to 留在句尾。

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: I spoke to 后置修饰 person，中文前移理解为“我交谈过的那个人”。
exampleNotes.detail: spoke 需要 to，关系词省略后 to 仍保留。

rules: 介词后可接 wh-从句等名词性结构作宾语。
口语疑问句中，介词常留在句尾，疑问词移到句首。
定语从句中介词可留在句尾；正式语体也可用 to whom 等“介词+关系词”。

questions.question: We talked about ___.
questions.correct: 介词后用陈述语序的 wh-从句。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：介词后用陈述语序的 wh-从句。

questions.question: 日常英语中哪句自然？
questions.correct: 日常表达常把介词 to 留在句尾。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：日常表达常把介词 to 留在句尾。

questions.question: 选择正确表达。
questions.correct: spoke 需要 to，关系词省略后 to 仍保留。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：spoke 需要 to，关系词省略后 to 仍保留。

narration.text: 介词后面不一定只有一个短名词，有时会带一整块信息。<#0.4#>We talked about what he said。<#0.8#>about 后面的 what he said 整体回答“谈论什么”，所以整块内容作为介词宾语，内部仍有自己的结构。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>Who are you talking to？<#0.8#>to 的对象是 Who，但疑问词被移到句首，介词留在句尾。这种位置变化不代表 to 没有对象。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The person I spoke to is here。<#0.8#>I spoke to 说明 The person，to 的对象由前面的 person 补回理解，介词同样可以留在从句末尾。<#0.8#>判断复杂介词宾语时，先找介词建立的关系，再追问对象是否被展开成 wh 从句，或因疑问、定语从句移到前面。把移走的对象在心里放回介词后，关系能闭合，就不要把句尾介词误判成多余。

lessons.title: 介词综合分析方法
lessons.meta: 关系、边界、功能三步判断
examples: The students in the library are reading.
The students are reading in the library.

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: 先判断 in the library 紧跟 students 并限定“哪些学生”，中文前移为“图书馆里的学生”。
exampleNotes.detail: 介词 in 和宾语 the library 构成整体。

exampleNotes.body: 它位于完整谓语后并说明动作地点。
Who 是 speak to 的介词宾语。

rules: 综合分析第一步先找介词和完整宾语，划出介词短语边界。
第二步判断介词短语与哪个成分建立关系，再确定句法功能。
第三步检查介词是否可能兼任连词、小品词或不定式标记，并结合后接结构验证。

questions.question: 本句介词短语的完整边界是什么？
questions.correct: 介词 in 和宾语 the library 构成整体。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：介词 in 和宾语 the library 构成整体。

questions.question: 这里 in the library 为什么是状语？

options.text: 它说明 reading 的地点

questions.correct: 它位于完整谓语后并说明动作地点。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：它位于完整谓语后并说明动作地点。

questions.question: 本句 to 为什么是介词？

options.text: 它与疑问词 Who 构成支配关系
它后面必须直接接动词原形

questions.correct: Who 是 speak to 的介词宾语。
questions.wrong: 再看规则：Who 是 speak to 的介词宾语。

narration.text: 同一个地点短语放在不同位置，会挂到不同对象上。先看。<#0.4#>The students in the library are reading。<#0.8#>句中的地点关系紧跟 students，回答“哪些学生”，所以它修饰名词，是后置定语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The students are reading in the library。<#0.8#>这次句子先出现完整动作 are reading，后面的地点关系回答“在哪里读”，所以它修饰动作，是地点状语。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Who are you speaking to？<#0.8#>to 虽在句尾，仍和句首 Who 建立说话对象关系，Who 是被移到前面的介词宾语。<#0.8#>综合判断按三步走：先找介词和它真正的对象，确定位置、时间或其他关系；再划清介词短语边界；最后看整个短语贴着名词作后置定语，挂在动作上作状语，还是补足中心词。若对象被前移，再把它放回去验证关系。

en.title: Prepositions · 25 lessons
en.copy: Master high-frequency essentials before complex structures.

course.title: Definition and core function
course.meta: Linking two elements through a relation
examples: The cup is on the table.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: on does not merely equal one translation; it relates the cup to the table surface.
after links met to lunch: the meeting happened after lunch.
with links spoke to her teacher: the teacher took part in the conversation.

rules: In “We met after lunch,” after links the meeting to lunch and places it later in time.
A preposition links an action or entity to a reference and expresses their relation.

questions.question: What relation does on establish?

options.text: A surface relation between the cup and table

questions.correct: on links cup and table in a surface relation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: on links cup and table in a surface relation.

questions.question: What is the time reference in “after lunch”?
questions.correct: lunch is the object and time reference.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: lunch is the object and time reference.

questions.question: What should be identified first when choosing a preposition?

options.text: The first Chinese translation that comes to mind

questions.correct: The relation type is more reliable than an isolated translation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The relation type is more reliable than an isolated translation.

narration.text:
先想一个画面：一只杯子放在桌面上。英语怎样让听的人知道，杯子和桌子是什么关系？<#0.7#>
The cup is on the table。<#0.8#>on 后面带着 the table，把桌子当成参照，再告诉我们杯子接触桌面。它没有增加一个新动作，只是在交代杯子在哪里。<#0.8#>
再换成时间。We met after lunch。<#0.7#>见面是主要事情，lunch 是时间参照。after 把见面放到午饭后面，让人知道两件事谁先谁后。这里不能只把 after 背成“在什么之后”，要看到它正在安排时间顺序。<#0.8#>
She spoke with her teacher。<#0.7#>说话是主要动作，her teacher 是另一个参与者。with 告诉我们，老师和她一起参与了交谈。它表达的是共同参与，不只是机械翻译成“和什么在一起”。<#0.8#>
像 on、after、with 这样的小词，会带出一个参照对象，再说明前面的事物或动作和这个参照对象有什么关系。这样的小词叫介词。介词后面的名词或代词叫介词宾语；介词和它后面的部分合在一起，叫介词短语。<#0.8#>
判断时做三件事：找到这个关系词；抓住它后面的参照对象；再问它交代的是位置、时间、方向、参与者，还是别的关系。先看关系，再看中文意思，介词就不会变成一堆零散翻译。

course.title: What prepositions are
examples: The game stopped because of the rain.
The cat came out of the box.

analyses.label: Complex prepositional phrase as reason adverbial

exampleNotes.body: after is the preposition; lunch is its object.
because of is a complex preposition taking a noun phrase.
out of plus the object the box forms a prepositional phrase.

rules: after is a one-word preposition and forms a phrase with lunch.
because of and in front of are multiword prepositions.
A preposition expresses a relation; together with its object it forms a prepositional phrase.

questions.question: What is the preposition in “after lunch”?
questions.correct: after is the preposition; lunch is its object.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: after is the preposition; lunch is its object.

questions.question: ___ the rain takes a noun phrase.
questions.correct: because of is a complex preposition taking a noun phrase.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: because of is a complex preposition taking a noun phrase.

questions.question: What is the whole unit “out of the box”?
questions.correct: out of plus the object the box forms a prepositional phrase.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: out of plus the object the box forms a prepositional phrase.

narration.text: 约好午饭后见面，页面第一句是。<#0.4#>We met after lunch。<#0.8#>after 只有一个词，后面带 lunch，把见面安排在午饭之后。这种单个词直接建立关系的，叫简单介词。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The game stopped because of the rain。<#0.8#>这里建立原因关系的部分由两个词组成，却要合起来理解，不能只拿其中一个词分析。这类整体叫复合介词。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The cat came out of the box。<#0.8#>这里的关系词组也要整体看，它从盒子内部出发，交代猫离开的起点。页面三组关系结构都是介词连同后面对象组成的介词短语。<#0.8#>本节只解决“介词长什么样”：它可能是一个词，也可能是几个词组成的固定整体。判断时先找后面的参照对象，再向前确认究竟由一个词还是一组词共同建立关系；一组词若缺一部分就失去原意，就按整体识别。

course.title: Prepositions and their objects

exampleNotes.body: Use object form me after a preposition.
A noun phrase can be the object.
Use a gerund after prepositional before.

rules: A preposition can take an object pronoun.
A preposition can take a noun phrase.
A verb after a preposition uses the -ing form.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: beside ___
questions.correct: Use object form me after a preposition.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use object form me after a preposition.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: about ___
questions.correct: A noun phrase can be the object.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: A noun phrase can be the object.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: before ___
questions.correct: Use a gerund after prepositional before.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use a gerund after prepositional before.

narration.text: 座位在谁旁边，要把那个人说出来。<#0.4#>She sat beside me。<#0.8#>beside 先给出“旁边”的关系，me 再提供参照对象。这里不能用 I，因为代词放在介词后面，要用宾格 me。这个被介词带出的对象，叫介词宾语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>We talked about the plan。<#0.8#>about 说明谈话围绕什么，the plan 是完整的名词短语，负责把话题补清楚。介词如果没有后面的对象，关系通常就悬空了。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Before leaving, he called me。<#0.8#>before 后面想放“离开”这个动作时，不能直接放动词原形，而要用 leaving。这里 leaving 把动作当成一件事情，作为介词宾语。<#0.8#>本节重点不是再认介词，而是看介词后面能放什么。操作时先圈介词，再圈紧跟它的完整对象：代词要用宾格，名词要把整个短语圈全，动作放在介词后通常用 ing 形式。

course.title: Prepositions, conjunctions and particles
course.meta: Identify the following unit and syntactic role
examples: I look forward to meeting you.

exampleNotes.body: before is followed by the noun phrase dinner, so it is a preposition here.
Here to is a preposition and takes the gerund meeting.
up forms a phrasal verb with look; the word is the object of look up.

rules: before is a preposition before a noun phrase and a conjunction before a clause.
Prepositional to takes a noun or gerund; infinitival to takes a base verb.
Items such as up in a phrasal verb are particles; a preposition introduces its own object and relation.

questions.question: What is before in “before we ate”?
questions.correct: we ate is a clause, so before is a conjunction.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: we ate is a clause, so before is a conjunction.

questions.question: look forward to ___ you
questions.correct: Here to is a preposition and takes the gerund meeting.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Here to is a preposition and takes the gerund meeting.

questions.question: What is up in “look up the word”?
questions.correct: up forms a phrasal verb with look; the word is the object of look up.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: up forms a phrasal verb with look; the word is the object of look up.

narration.text: 同一个小词，换了后面的结构，工作可能完全不同。先看。<#0.4#>Before dinner, we walked。<#0.8#>before 后面直接带名词 dinner，合起来说明 walked 发生的时间，所以这里 before 是介词。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>I look forward to meeting you。<#0.8#>这里 to 后面接 meeting，表示期待指向的事情。to 属于 look forward to 这个关系结构中的介词，所以后面的动作要用 ing 形式，不能因为看到 to 就自动判断为不定式标记。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Please look up the word。<#0.8#>up 后面没有自己的介词宾语，它和 look 合起来表达“查找”，the word 是整个 look up 的宾语。这里 up 叫小品词。<#0.8#>判断边界时，先看小词后面有没有名词、代词或 ing 形式作为自己的对象；有对象并建立关系，通常按介词分析。若后面接完整分句，可能是连词；若和动词合成整体、没有自己的对象，就考虑小品词。

course.title: Prepositions of time
course.meta: at · on · in and time ranges
examples: The library is open from nine to five.

exampleNotes.body: Use at with clock time.
Use on with days.
Use in with seasons.
Use from...to for a range.
Use since for a starting point.
Use for with a duration.

rules: Use at for clock times and precise points.
Use on for days and dates.
Use in for months, seasons, years and longer periods.
from...to expresses a start-to-end range.
since marks a starting point extending to the present.
for expresses a duration.

questions.question: Which preposition goes before six o’clock?
questions.correct: Use at with clock time.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use at with clock time.

questions.question: Which preposition goes before Monday?
questions.correct: Use on with days.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use on with days.

questions.question: Which preposition goes before spring?
questions.correct: Use in with seasons.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use in with seasons.

questions.question: The opening hours run ___ nine ___ five.
questions.correct: Use from...to for a range.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use from...to for a range.

questions.question: She has lived here ___ 2020.
questions.correct: Use since for a starting point.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use since for a starting point.

questions.question: We waited ___ two hours.
questions.correct: Use for with a duration.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use for with a duration.

narration.text: 安排日程时，先看时间像一个点、一页日历，还是一段较长的范围。<#0.4#>The class starts at six。<#0.8#>six 是钟表上的具体时刻，所以用 at。<#0.5#>We meet on Monday。<#0.8#>Monday 是日历上的一天，所以用 on。<#0.5#>Birds return in spring。<#0.8#>spring 是包住许多天的一段季节，所以用 in。<#0.7#>接着看起止。<#0.4#>The library is open from nine to five。<#0.8#>from 标出起点，to 标出终点，两边合起来画出开放的时间范围。<#0.7#>She has lived here since 2020 里，since 把 2020 当成起点，并把状态拉到现在；We waited for two hours 里，for 不说从哪天开始，只量出持续了两小时。<#0.8#>本节把基础时间关系放进一张图。判断时先问：是具体时刻、某一天，还是较长时段；再看句子要的是起点、终点还是持续长度。点钟选 at，日期和星期选 on，月份季节年份等选 in；起止、起点和时长再分别检查 from to、since、for。

course.title: Endpoints, periods and deadlines
examples: Please finish the work by Friday.
No phones rang during the meeting.

exampleNotes.body: Use by for a deadline.
Use until for continuation to an endpoint.
during places rang within the period of the meeting: no phones rang in that period.

rules: by means no later than a time and marks a deadline.
until marks how long an action or state continues.
during takes an event or period noun; within means before a limited period ends.

questions.question: Finish it no later than Friday: finish it ___ Friday
questions.correct: Use by for a deadline.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use by for a deadline.

questions.question: We continued waiting up to noon: waited ___ noon
questions.correct: Use until for continuation to an endpoint.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use until for continuation to an endpoint.

questions.question: Reply before the two-hour limit ends: reply ___ two hours
questions.correct: Use within for a limited period.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use within for a limited period.

narration.text: 任务写着周五前交，重点不是一直做到周五，而是最晚不能超过周五。<#0.4#>Please finish the work by Friday。<#0.8#>by 给出截止线，周五之前任何时候完成都可以。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>We waited until noon。<#0.8#>until 让 waited 这个动作持续到中午，中午是等待停止的终点。by 关心“最迟何时完成”，until 关心“状态一直延续到何时”。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>No phones rang during the meeting。<#0.8#>during 把 rang 放进 meeting 这段期间，说明整场会议之中没有电话响；它只标期间，不直接说明动作持续多久。within 则常表示必须落在给定期限内部。<#0.8#>判断时先看动作类型：是要在某条线之前完成，用 by；是一直维持到终点，用 until；是说某事件发生在一段活动中，用 during；是限定在多长时间以内，用 within。先画时间线，再选词。

course.title: Common time contrasts
course.meta: in · after · on time · in time
examples: The train will leave in ten minutes.
We arrived in time for the bus.

analyses.label: Time after a past reference point

exampleNotes.body: Use in for a future point measured from now.
Use after when measuring from a stated reference point.
Use in time for early enough.

rules: in + duration refers to a future point measured from now.
after + duration is normally measured from a past or contextual reference point.
on time means punctually; in time means early enough.

questions.question: The train leaves ten minutes from now: leave ___ ten minutes
questions.correct: Use in for a future point measured from now.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use in for a future point measured from now.

questions.question: He returned two days after leaving: returned ___ two days
questions.correct: Use after when measuring from a stated reference point.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use after when measuring from a stated reference point.

questions.question: We arrived early enough for the bus: arrived ___ for the bus
questions.correct: Use in time for early enough.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use in time for early enough.

narration.text: 两天以后和两天之内，中文听着接近，英语看的时间起点不同。先看。<#0.4#>The train will leave in ten minutes。<#0.8#>in ten minutes 从“现在”往后数十分钟，表示十分钟后列车将离开，常和将来情境连用。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>He returned after two days。<#0.8#>after two days 是从语境中已经确定的某个事件起，再过两天返回。它不一定以说话此刻为起点。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>We arrived in time for the bus。<#0.8#>in time 表示赶在错过之前到达，虽然可能不早，但还来得及；on time 则强调正好按计划时间，不迟到。<#0.8#>判断时先找计时起点：从现在往后多久，多考虑 in；从前文事件之后多久，用 after。再看重点是“准点”还是“还来得及”：按时刻表是 on time，赶上最后机会是 in time。

course.title: Prepositions of place
examples: The keys are in the box.
A picture hangs above the desk.
The cup is on the table.
The valley lies below the village.
A lamp hangs over the table.

exampleNotes.body: Use at for a point.
Use in for an interior.
above means higher, not touching a surface.
Use on for surface contact.
below means lower than.
over commonly means directly above.

rules: at marks a place as a point.
in marks an interior.
on marks contact with a surface.
above/below mean higher or lower without requiring direct alignment.
over/under commonly mean directly above or below.

questions.question: Wait ___ the gate
questions.correct: Use at for a point.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use at for a point.

questions.question: Inside the box: ___ the box
questions.correct: Use in for an interior.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use in for an interior.

questions.question: Higher than the desk without contact: ___ the desk
questions.correct: above means higher, not touching a surface.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: above means higher, not touching a surface.

questions.question: The cup touches the surface: ___ the table
questions.correct: Use on for surface contact.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use on for surface contact.

questions.question: Lower than the village without direct alignment
questions.correct: below means lower than.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: below means lower than.

questions.question: The lamp is directly above the table
questions.correct: over commonly means directly above.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: over commonly means directly above.

narration.text: 找东西时，先决定把地点看成一个点、一个内部空间，还是一个接触面。<#0.4#>Tom waited at the gate。<#0.8#>at 把 gate 当作等待发生的点位。<#0.5#>The keys are in the box。<#0.8#>in 强调钥匙在盒子内部。<#0.7#>A picture hangs above the desk 里，above 只说明画比桌子高，不要求正对；The cup is on the table 里，on 还表示杯子接触桌面。<#0.7#>The valley lies below the village 中，below 表示山谷位置更低；A lamp hangs over the table 中，over 常让人看到灯在桌子上方覆盖或正对的画面。相应地，under 常用于正下方。<#0.8#>本节解决静态位置的基础视角。判断时先问：参照物被当成点、内部还是表面；再比较高低位置是否要求正对或覆盖。点位用 at，内部用 in，接触面用 on；单纯高低看 above、below，正上正下或覆盖关系再考虑 over、under。

course.title: Precise relative position
examples: The bank is between the school and the park.

analyses.text: between the school and the park.
analyses.label: Place adverbial between two points

exampleNotes.body: Use between for two distinct places.
Use among within a group.
Use beside for next to.

rules: between relates two or clearly separate individual items.
among means within a group viewed collectively.
beside means next to; besides means in addition to.

questions.question: The bank is ___ the school and the park.
questions.correct: Use between for two distinct places.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use between for two distinct places.

questions.question: She stood ___ the crowd.
questions.correct: Use among within a group.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use among within a group.

questions.question: Ben sat next to me: sat ___ me
questions.correct: Use beside for next to.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use beside for next to.

narration.text: 描述位置时，“在中间”和“在旁边”最容易被中文带偏。先看。<#0.4#>The bank is between the school and the park。<#0.8#>学校和公园是两个清楚分开的参照，银行位于二者之间，所以用 between。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She stood among the crowd。<#0.8#>crowd 是一群围绕她的人，重点是处在群体之中，而不是精确夹在两个对象之间，所以用 among。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Ben sat beside me。<#0.8#>beside 只表示 Ben 坐在我旁边。besides 多了 s 时，常表示“除……之外还包括”，不是空间上的旁边。<#0.8#>判断时先数参照关系：两个或几个分别明确列出的对象之间，用 between；处在未逐个列出的群体之中，用 among。再分清 beside 和 besides：一个说位置相邻，一个说范围追加。不要只凭中文都能译成“在……中”或“除外”来选。

course.title: Direction and movement
examples: The cat jumped onto the table.
The train went through the tunnel.

exampleNotes.body: into marks movement inward.
onto marks movement to a surface.
across means from one side to the other.
through marks movement within an interior.

rules: in/on mark static position; into/onto mark movement to a position.
through marks movement within an enclosed space.
across marks movement from one side of a surface or area to another.

questions.question: Walk to the inside: walk ___ the room
questions.correct: into marks movement inward.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: into marks movement inward.

questions.question: Jump to the surface: jump ___ the table
questions.correct: onto marks movement to a surface.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: onto marks movement to a surface.

questions.question: Run from one side of the road to the other
questions.correct: across means from one side to the other.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: across means from one side to the other.

questions.question: Move within the tunnel from end to end
questions.correct: through marks movement within an interior.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: through marks movement within an interior.

narration.text: 位置课回答“在哪里”，这一课回答“从哪里动到哪里”。<#0.4#>She walked into the room。<#0.8#>into 把走路的终点放到房间内部，既有方向，也有进入。<#0.5#>The cat jumped onto the table。<#0.8#>onto 表示猫跳动后到达桌面，并与表面接触。单说 in 或 on，通常只描写静态位置。<#0.7#>We ran across the road 中，across 画的是从道路一边横到另一边；The train went through the tunnel 中，through 画的是进入隧道内部，再从内部穿过。<#0.8#>to 只指向目标，不一定说明已经进入内部或落到表面；into 和 onto 把终点关系说得更具体。<#0.7#>判断运动介词，先找动作轨迹和终点：进入内部选 into，到达表面选 onto；横过一个表面或区域选 across，穿过有内部的空间选 through。最后检查句子是在说动态到达，还是已经处于 in、on 表示的位置。

course.title: Movement paths
examples: The hikers went through the forest.

exampleNotes.body: Use along for following a route.
Use past for movement beyond a point.
Use through for movement within an interior.

rules: along marks movement following a line or route.
past marks movement beyond a person or place.
across crosses a surface or area; through passes inside an enclosed space.

questions.question: Walk following the river: walk ___ the river
questions.correct: Use along for following a route.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use along for following a route.

questions.question: Run beyond the library: run ___ the library
questions.correct: Use past for movement beyond a point.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use past for movement beyond a point.

questions.question: Pass inside the forest: go ___ the forest
questions.correct: Use through for movement within an interior.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use through for movement within an interior.

narration.text: 走路导航不仅要说终点，还要说一路怎样经过。<#0.4#>We walked along the river。<#0.8#>along 把路线贴着河流延伸，重点是沿着同一方向前进，不要求跨到河对岸。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She ran past the library。<#0.8#>past 把图书馆当成路上的参照点，她从它旁边经过并继续向前，重点是“超过、经过”这个点。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The hikers went through the forest。<#0.8#>through 表示徒步者进入森林内部，并沿内部路径穿行。across 则更强调从一个区域的一边到另一边。<#0.8#>判断路径时先画一条线：路线顺着某个线状参照延伸，用 along；越过路边的一个点，用 past；进入并穿行于空间内部，用 through；若重点是横跨表面或区域，再考虑 across。每个词回答的是轨迹形状，不只是“经过”的中文翻译。

course.title: Sources and separation
examples: The bird flew out of the cage.
The cup fell off the table.

exampleNotes.body: Use from for origin.
Use out of for movement from an interior.
Use off for movement away from a surface.

rules: from marks a source, origin or starting point.
out of marks movement from inside to outside.
off marks movement away from a surface.

questions.question: This train comes ___ Beijing.
questions.correct: Use from for origin.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use from for origin.

questions.question: The bird flew from inside the cage to outside.
questions.correct: Use out of for movement from an interior.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use out of for movement from an interior.

questions.question: The cup fell away from the table surface.
questions.correct: Use off for movement away from a surface.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use off for movement away from a surface.

narration.text: 运动不只看去向，也能回头看从哪里出发、从哪里脱离。<#0.4#>This train comes from Beijing。<#0.8#>from 把 Beijing 标成列车来源或起点，但不额外说明它原来在什么容器里。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The bird flew out of the cage。<#0.8#>out of 明确画出鸟原来在笼子内部，飞行后离开内部空间。它比单独的 from 多了“从里面出来”的画面。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The cup fell off the table。<#0.8#>off 说明杯子原来与桌面有接触，掉落后脱离这个表面。<#0.8#>判断时先问起点是什么关系：只交代来源或出发点，用 from；原来在内部、现在离开内部，用 out of；原来接触表面、现在脱离表面，用 off。把动作前后的两个位置都画出来，就不会把三个词都机械翻成“从”。

course.title: Means, instrument and agent
examples: She cut the paper with scissors.
The novel was written by Orwell.

exampleNotes.body: Use by for transport.
Use with for an instrument.
Use by for the agent.

rules: by + transport expresses the means of travel.
with + an instrument identifies the tool used.
In a passive clause, by introduces the agent.

questions.question: By train: ___ train
questions.correct: Use by for transport.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use by for transport.

questions.question: Using scissors: ___ scissors
questions.correct: Use with for an instrument.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use with for an instrument.

questions.question: Painted ___ Monet
questions.correct: Use by for the agent.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use by for the agent.

narration.text: 同样译成“用”或“由”，英语会区分交通方式、手里的工具和动作执行者。<#0.4#>We travelled by train。<#0.8#>by train 把 train 当成出行方式，不是在强调某一列具体火车内部。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She cut the paper with scissors。<#0.8#>scissors 是她实际拿来剪纸的工具，所以用 with。这里动作执行者是 She，工具是 scissors，两者不能混。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The novel was written by Orwell。<#0.8#>句子把 novel 放在主语位置，was written 是被动结构，by Orwell 再补出写作动作由谁完成。这个 Orwell 叫施事，也就是动作执行者。<#0.8#>判断时先问后面的名词扮演什么角色：交通工具作为方式，用 by；手里使用的具体器具，用 with；被动句中补出谁做了动作，也用 by。不要只看中文都有一个“用”字。

course.title: Medium, language and presentation

exampleNotes.body: Use by email for the means of transmission.
Use on with the medium TV.
Use in with a language.

rules: by can mark a means of transmission, as in by email.
on is common with media such as TV, radio, the phone and online platforms.
in can mark language, colour, ink or form of presentation.

questions.question: Send it using email: send it ___ email
questions.correct: Use by email for the means of transmission.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use by email for the means of transmission.

questions.question: The match is broadcast ___ TV.
questions.correct: Use on with the medium TV.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use on with the medium TV.

questions.question: Answer using English: answer ___ English
questions.correct: Use in with a language.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use in with a language.

narration.text: 发送消息、观看比赛、选择回答语言，都在说“通过什么呈现”，但关系不完全一样。<#0.4#>Please send it by email。<#0.8#>email 在这里是传递信息的渠道，by 强调通过这种方式发送。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The match is on TV。<#0.8#>on TV 表示比赛出现在电视这个传播平台上，重点是内容在哪个平台播出。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>She answered in English。<#0.8#>in English 说明回答采用的语言或表达形式，不是交通方式，也不是平台。<#0.8#>本节与上一课的工具关系相邻，但它专门区分媒介、平台和语言。判断时问三个问题：是在说信息通过什么渠道送出，内容在哪个平台呈现，还是用哪种语言或形式表达？渠道方式常用 by，平台常用 on，语言和表达形式常用 in。

course.title: Cause, purpose and concession
examples: The match stopped because of the rain.
This tool is for cutting glass.
We stayed home because it rained.
In spite of being tired, she continued.

exampleNotes.body: the rain is a noun phrase, so use because of.
for expresses purpose or use.
despite takes a gerund and marks concession.
Use because before a complete clause.
in spite of can take a gerund to mark concession.

rules: because of takes a noun phrase and expresses reason.
because takes a complete clause and expresses reason.
for + a noun or gerund can express use or purpose.
despite takes a noun or gerund and marks concession.
in spite of takes a noun or gerund and marks concession.

questions.question: ___ the rain, we stayed home.
questions.correct: the rain is a noun phrase, so use because of.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: the rain is a noun phrase, so use because of.

questions.question: This knife is ___ cutting bread.
questions.correct: for expresses purpose or use.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: for expresses purpose or use.

questions.question: ___ being tired, she worked.
questions.correct: despite takes a gerund and marks concession.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: despite takes a gerund and marks concession.

questions.question: ___ it rained, we stayed home.
questions.correct: Use because before a complete clause.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use because before a complete clause.

questions.question: ___ being tired, she continued.
questions.correct: in spite of can take a gerund to mark concession.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: in spite of can take a gerund to mark concession.

narration.text: 比赛为什么停、工具拿来做什么、天气虽冷还是否继续，是三种不同逻辑。<#0.4#>The match stopped because of the rain。<#0.8#>because of 后面带名词 the rain，把雨作为停止的原因。<#0.5#>This tool is for cutting glass。<#0.8#>for cutting glass 不说已经发生的动作，而是说明工具的用途。<#0.7#>Despite the cold, they continued 里，despite 承认寒冷这个阻碍，但主句结果仍然继续，这叫让步关系。<#0.7#>再对比。<#0.4#>We stayed home because it rained。<#0.8#>because 后面是 it rained 这个完整分句；because of 后面则是名词短语。最后看 In spite of being tired, she continued，in spite of 和 despite 一样建立让步，但它是三个词组成的整体，后面用 being tired。<#0.8#>判断时先分逻辑：解释原因、说明用途，还是承认阻碍仍有结果；再看后面接名词短语、ing 形式还是完整分句。原因短语用 because of，完整原因句用 because；用途看 for；让步看 despite 或 in spite of。

course.title: Material, role and exclusion
course.meta: of · from · like · as · except · besides
examples: The table is made of wood.

exampleNotes.body: The wood remains recognizable in the table, so made of identifies the visible material.
Use as for an actual role.
Use except to exclude Tom.

rules: made of keeps the material recognizable; made from suggests transformation.
like means similar to; as marks an actual role, identity or use.
except excludes; besides adds another included item.

questions.question: Paper is produced by transforming wood: Paper is made ___ wood.
questions.correct: Wood is transformed into paper, so use made from.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Wood is transformed into paper, so use made from.

questions.question: Her actual job is a doctor: works ___ a doctor
questions.correct: Use as for an actual role.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use as for an actual role.

questions.question: Everyone came but Tom did not: ___ Tom
questions.correct: Use except to exclude Tom.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use except to exclude Tom.

narration.text: 看一张木桌，木头的样子仍然看得出来。<#0.4#>The table is made of wood。<#0.8#>of 把成品和仍可辨认的材料连起来，说明桌子的构成。若原料加工后已经看不出原样，通常会用另一种来源关系表达，本节先抓住“材料仍可辨认”这条线。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She works as a doctor。<#0.8#>as a doctor 说明她实际以医生的身份工作，不是在说她像医生。like 更偏向相似，as 更强调真实身份或承担的角色。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Everyone came except Tom。<#0.8#>except 把 Tom 从 everyone 所包含的范围中排除，意思是其他人都来了。besides 则常把对象继续加进范围，方向相反。<#0.8#>判断时先找本节的三类关系：成品由什么材料构成，某人以什么身份行动，某对象是被排除还是被追加。材料看构成关系，身份区分 as 与相似的 like，范围区分排除的 except 与追加的 besides。

course.title: Topic, content and features
examples: A lecture on climate change begins now.
The girl with glasses is Amy.

exampleNotes.body: Use about for a general topic.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: on climate change follows lecture; Chinese normally moves it before 讲座.
exampleNotes.detail: Use on for a formal subject.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: with glasses follows girl; Chinese moves it before 女孩.
exampleNotes.detail: Use with for possession of a feature.

rules: about marks a general topic; on often marks a formal or specialist topic.
on can mark the formal subject of a book, lecture or article.
of often marks relation, composition or content; with marks possession or a feature.

questions.question: We talked generally ___ the trip.
questions.correct: Use about for a general topic.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use about for a general topic.

questions.question: A formal lecture whose subject is science: a lecture ___ science
questions.correct: Use on for a formal subject.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use on for a formal subject.

questions.question: The girl who has glasses: the girl ___ glasses
questions.correct: Use with for possession of a feature.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use with for possession of a feature.

narration.text: 谈话围绕旅行、讲座聚焦气候变化、女孩带着眼镜，这三句都在名词或动作旁补信息，却建立不同关系。<#0.4#>We talked about the trip。<#0.8#>about the trip 说明谈话围绕什么话题，修补的是 talked 的内容范围。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>A lecture on climate change begins now。<#0.8#>on climate change 紧跟 lecture，告诉我们讲座的专题，语气通常比普通谈话的 about 更聚焦、正式。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The girl with glasses is Amy。<#0.8#>with glasses 不是谈话内容，而是给 girl 增加外在特征，帮助听者认出是哪位女孩。<#0.8#>判断时先问短语靠着谁、在补什么：围绕动作的谈论内容常用 about；讲座、文章等聚焦的专题可用 on；给人物或事物附加“带有什么”的特征，用 with。不要因为中文都能出现“关于、有”就混选。

course.title: Prepositional phrases as adverbials
course.meta: Modifying an action, state or clause
examples: The children played in the garden.
She opened the box with a key.

exampleNotes.body: It states when the meeting happens.
It states where the children played.
with introduces the instrument key.

rules: A prepositional phrase functions as a time adverbial when it locates the action in time.
A prepositional phrase functions as a place adverbial when it locates the action in space.
A prepositional phrase can also express manner, instrument, reason, purpose, condition or concession.

questions.question: What does after class modify?
questions.correct: It states when the meeting happens.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It states when the meeting happens.

questions.question: What is in the garden?
questions.correct: It states where the children played.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It states where the children played.

questions.question: What does with a key express?
questions.correct: with introduces the instrument key.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: with introduces the instrument key.

narration.text: 同一个动作说清以后，还可以补上什么时候、在哪里、用什么方式发生。<#0.4#>We will meet after class。<#0.8#>主干 We will meet 已经说明谁要见面，after class 只给 meet 加上时间，这整个介词短语叫时间状语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The children played in the garden。<#0.8#>in the garden 回答“在哪里玩”，修饰的是动作 played，所以是地点状语，不是 children 的种类。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>She opened the box with a key。<#0.8#>with a key 回答“用什么打开”，给动作增加工具关系，属于工具状语。<#0.8#>本节解决介词短语怎样挂到动作上。判断时先暂时拿掉介词短语，看句子主干是否仍成立；再问它是在补时间、地点、工具、原因还是方式。若它主要回答动作何时、何地、怎样发生，整体就按状语分析。

course.title: Prepositional phrases as postmodifiers
course.meta: English after the noun; Chinese before it
examples: The boy with a red cap is my brother.
The books on the desk are mine.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: with a red cap follows boy; Chinese moves it before 男孩.
exampleNotes.detail: The phrase follows the head noun.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: on the desk follows books but precedes 书 in Chinese.
exampleNotes.detail: It modifies books.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: from Class Two moves before 学生 in Chinese.
exampleNotes.detail: It identifies Students.

rules: A prepositional phrase directly after a noun acts as a postmodifier when it identifies that noun.
A postmodifier modifies a noun; a place adverbial modifies a verb.

questions.question: Which order means “the boy wearing a red cap”?

options.text: the with a red cap boy
the boy with a red cap

questions.correct: The phrase follows the head noun.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The phrase follows the head noun.

questions.question: What is on the desk in “The books on the desk are mine”?
questions.correct: It modifies books.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It modifies books.

questions.question: What does from Class Two modify?
questions.correct: It identifies Students.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It identifies Students.

narration.text: 人群里要认出戴红帽子的男孩，英语先说男孩，再把特征放在后面。<#0.4#>The boy with a red cap is my brother。<#0.8#>with a red cap 紧跟 boy，帮助确定是哪一个男孩，所以整个短语修饰名词 boy，叫后置定语。中文通常把它移到名词前理解。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The books on the desk are mine。<#0.8#>on the desk 贴着 books，回答“哪些书”，不是在说明 are 发生在哪里。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Students from Class Two won。<#0.8#>from Class Two 限定 Students 的来源，确定获胜的是二班学生。<#0.8#>判断时先看介词短语是否紧跟名词，再问它在回答“哪一个、哪一些、什么样的”。若删掉后名词范围变宽，它通常是后置定语；若主要回答动作在哪里发生，则是地点状语。最后翻成中文时可把这段说明前移，但英语结构仍在名词后。

course.title: Prepositional phrases as predicatives
course.meta: Following a linking verb to describe the subject
examples: The keys are on the desk.

exampleNotes.body: It follows are and locates the keys.
It describes the subject’s state.
worked is an action predicate; the phrase adds place.

rules: A prepositional phrase can be predicative when it follows a linking verb and describes the subject.
A predicative prepositional phrase can express an abstract state, not only location.
To distinguish predicative from adverbial, check whether the preceding verb is linking or an action verb.

questions.question: What is on the desk in this sentence?
questions.correct: It follows are and locates the keys.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It follows are and locates the keys.

questions.question: What does in danger describe?
questions.correct: It describes the subject’s state.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: It describes the subject’s state.

questions.question: What is in the library in “She worked in the library”?
questions.correct: worked is an action predicate; the phrase adds place.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: worked is an action predicate; the phrase adds place.

narration.text: 钥匙在哪里，句子可以直接用一段位置关系来回答。<#0.4#>The keys are on the desk。<#0.8#>are 像一座桥，on the desk 放在桥后说明主语 keys 所处的位置。整个介词短语在这里叫表语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The child is in danger。<#0.8#>in danger 不是真实空间内部，而是说明孩子处于危险状态；它仍通过 is 描写主语，所以也是表语。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>She worked in the library。<#0.8#>这里 worked 本身已经是完整动作，in the library 只补充工作地点，属于地点状语，不是表语。<#0.8#>判断时先看介词短语前面的动词：如果是 be 等系动词，短语直接说明主语在哪里或处于什么状态，按表语分析；如果前面是 worked 这类实义动作，短语只回答动作发生地点，通常是状语。不能只因位置在句尾就下结论。

course.title: Prepositional complements
examples: She is proud of her work.
The need for change is clear.

exampleNotes.body: depend selects on as its complement.
proud takes of.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: for change completes need; Chinese expresses it before 需要.
exampleNotes.detail: reason commonly takes for when naming what it explains.

rules: Some verbs require a selected prepositional complement, as in depend on.
Adjectives can select prepositional complements, as in proud of.
Nouns can take complements that specify their content, as in need for and reason for.

questions.question: Success depends ___ effort.
questions.correct: depend selects on as its complement.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: depend selects on as its complement.

questions.question: She is proud ___ her work.
questions.correct: proud takes of.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: proud takes of.

questions.question: the reason ___ the delay
questions.correct: reason commonly takes for when naming what it explains.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: reason commonly takes for when naming what it explains.

narration.text: 有些词说到一半，会让人自然追问“依靠什么、为哪件事骄傲、对什么的需要”。介词短语负责把这种未完成的关系补齐。<#0.4#>Success depends on effort。<#0.8#>depends 会追问依靠什么，on effort 是动词需要的补足成分。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She is proud of her work。<#0.8#>proud 只说“骄傲”还没有交代对象，of her work 补清骄傲所针对的事情，所以补足形容词 proud。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The need for change is clear。<#0.8#>for change 紧跟名词 need，说明是什么方面的需要，补足名词意义。<#0.8#>本节与普通状语不同：状语多是可选背景，补足成分由前面的中心词强烈要求。判断时先找介词短语前的动词、形容词或名词，再问去掉短语后是否留下“对谁、关于什么、依靠什么”的明显空缺；有空缺，就按相应中心词的补足成分分析。

course.title: Head words and preposition relations
examples: The answer to the question is clear.

exampleNotes.body: to directs the listening toward music.
in places the interest within the field of science.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: to the question follows answer; Chinese places it before 答案.
exampleNotes.detail: to makes the answer point to and correspond to the question.

rules: In listen to, to directs attention toward the object of listening.
In interested in, in places the interest within a field or area.
In answer to, to makes the answer point to and correspond to the question.
to commonly points an action or entity toward a target; in commonly places it within a field or area.
Relational meaning explains the choice, while usage conventions still need to be learned with the head word.

questions.question: listen ___ music
questions.correct: to directs the listening toward music.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: to directs the listening toward music.

questions.question: be interested ___ science
questions.correct: in places the interest within the field of science.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: in places the interest within the field of science.

questions.question: the answer ___ the question
questions.correct: to makes the answer point to and correspond to the question.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: to makes the answer point to and correspond to the question.

narration.text: 介词选择不是随便跟在词后，也不只是死背。先看。<#0.4#>She listens to music。<#0.8#>to 把听的注意方向引向 music，补清 listens 的目标。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>He is interested in science。<#0.8#>in 把兴趣放进 science 这个领域，说明兴趣所在的范围。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The answer to the question is clear。<#0.8#>to the question 放在 answer 后，让答案指向并对应那个问题。中文会把它前移理解，但英语把关系放在中心名词后。<#0.8#>本节开始研究中心词为什么选择某个介词：to 常有指向目标的感觉，in 常有处在领域或范围中的感觉。判断时先找中心词是动词、形容词还是名词，再问它要把关系指向目标、放入范围，还是建立对应；用关系帮助理解后，仍要把中心词和介词作为真实组合核对记忆。

course.title: Prepositions change relational meaning

exampleNotes.body: Use agree with for a person.
Use agree on for the matter settled.
Use agree to for consenting to a proposal.

rules: agree with takes a person or view and means share the same opinion.
agree on takes a topic or arrangement and means reach agreement about it.
agree to takes a plan, terms or proposal and means consent.

questions.question: agree ___ you
questions.correct: Use agree with for a person.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use agree with for a person.

questions.question: agree ___ the date
questions.correct: Use agree on for the matter settled.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use agree on for the matter settled.

questions.question: agree ___ the proposal
questions.correct: Use agree to for consenting to a proposal.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use agree to for consenting to a proposal.

narration.text: 同一个 agree，后面的介词一换，谈的对象类型也会变化。<#0.4#>I agree with you。<#0.8#>with 把我和 you 放进同一意见关系，表示我赞同你这个人表达的看法。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>We agreed on the date。<#0.8#>on the date 把 date 当成双方讨论后共同确定的事项，重点是就日期达成一致。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>They agreed to the plan。<#0.8#>to the plan 表示他们把同意指向这个方案，接受方案本身。<#0.8#>本节不是再背三个搭配，而是观察介词怎样改变 agree 后的关系：with 常连意见一致的人，on 常连协商确定的事项，to 常连被接受的建议或方案。判断时先辨认后面是人、共同议定事项，还是需要接受的内容；再选介词，并把整个关系放回语境检查。

course.title: Complex objects and stranded prepositions
examples: We talked about what he said.
The person I spoke to is here.

analyses.label: Wh-clause as object of a preposition
Relative clause with omitted object relative

exampleNotes.body: Use statement order in the wh-clause after a preposition.
Everyday English commonly strands to at the end.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: I spoke to follows person; Chinese moves the modifier before 人.
exampleNotes.detail: spoke requires to, which remains when the object relative is omitted.

rules: A preposition can take a nominal wh-clause as its object.
In ordinary questions, the preposition commonly remains at the end while its wh-word moves to the front.
A relative clause may strand the preposition; formal style may use preposition + relative word, such as to whom.

questions.question: We talked about ___.
questions.correct: Use statement order in the wh-clause after a preposition.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use statement order in the wh-clause after a preposition.

questions.question: Which is natural in everyday English?
questions.correct: Everyday English commonly strands to at the end.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Everyday English commonly strands to at the end.

questions.question: Choose the correct expression.
questions.correct: spoke requires to, which remains when the object relative is omitted.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: spoke requires to, which remains when the object relative is omitted.

narration.text: 介词后面不一定只有一个短名词，有时会带一整块信息。<#0.4#>We talked about what he said。<#0.8#>about 后面的 what he said 整体回答“谈论什么”，所以整块内容作为介词宾语，内部仍有自己的结构。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>Who are you talking to？<#0.8#>to 的对象是 Who，但疑问词被移到句首，介词留在句尾。这种位置变化不代表 to 没有对象。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The person I spoke to is here。<#0.8#>I spoke to 说明 The person，to 的对象由前面的 person 补回理解，介词同样可以留在从句末尾。<#0.8#>判断复杂介词宾语时，先找介词建立的关系，再追问对象是否被展开成 wh 从句，或因疑问、定语从句移到前面。把移走的对象在心里放回介词后，关系能闭合，就不要把句尾介词误判成多余。

course.title: Integrated preposition analysis
examples: The students in the library are reading.
The students are reading in the library.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: in the library follows and identifies students; Chinese moves it before 学生.
exampleNotes.detail: in plus the object the library forms the full phrase.

exampleNotes.body: It follows the complete predicate and locates the action.
Who is the object governed by to.

rules: First locate the preposition and its full object to mark the phrase boundary.
Next identify which element the phrase relates to, then determine its syntactic function.
Finally check whether the form is a preposition, conjunction, particle or infinitival marker by inspecting what follows.

questions.correct: Who is the object governed by to.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Who is the object governed by to.

narration.text: 同一个地点短语放在不同位置，会挂到不同对象上。先看。<#0.4#>The students in the library are reading。<#0.8#>句中的地点关系紧跟 students，回答“哪些学生”，所以它修饰名词，是后置定语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The students are reading in the library。<#0.8#>这次句子先出现完整动作 are reading，后面的地点关系回答“在哪里读”，所以它修饰动作，是地点状语。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Who are you speaking to？<#0.8#>to 虽在句尾，仍和句首 Who 建立说话对象关系，Who 是被移到前面的介词宾语。<#0.8#>综合判断按三步走：先找介词和它真正的对象，确定位置、时间或其他关系；再划清介词短语边界；最后看整个短语贴着名词作后置定语，挂在动作上作状语，还是补足中心词。若对象被前移，再把它放回去验证关系。

lessons.title: Definition and core function
lessons.meta: Linking two elements through a relation
examples: The cup is on the table.

exampleNotes.title: Rule focus
exampleNotes.body: on does not merely equal one translation; it relates the cup to the table surface.
after links met to lunch: the meeting happened after lunch.
with links spoke to her teacher: the teacher took part in the conversation.

rules: In “We met after lunch,” after links the meeting to lunch and places it later in time.
A preposition links an action or entity to a reference and expresses their relation.

questions.question: What relation does on establish?

options.text: A surface relation between the cup and table

questions.correct: on links cup and table in a surface relation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: on links cup and table in a surface relation.

questions.question: What is the time reference in “after lunch”?
questions.correct: lunch is the object and time reference.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: lunch is the object and time reference.

questions.question: What should be identified first when choosing a preposition?

options.text: The first Chinese translation that comes to mind

questions.correct: The relation type is more reliable than an isolated translation.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: The relation type is more reliable than an isolated translation.

narration.text:
先想一个画面：一只杯子放在桌面上。英语怎样让听的人知道，杯子和桌子是什么关系？<#0.7#>
The cup is on the table。<#0.8#>on 后面带着 the table，把桌子当成参照，再告诉我们杯子接触桌面。它没有增加一个新动作，只是在交代杯子在哪里。<#0.8#>
再换成时间。We met after lunch。<#0.7#>见面是主要事情，lunch 是时间参照。after 把见面放到午饭后面，让人知道两件事谁先谁后。这里不能只把 after 背成“在什么之后”，要看到它正在安排时间顺序。<#0.8#>
She spoke with her teacher。<#0.7#>说话是主要动作，her teacher 是另一个参与者。with 告诉我们，老师和她一起参与了交谈。它表达的是共同参与，不只是机械翻译成“和什么在一起”。<#0.8#>
像 on、after、with 这样的小词，会带出一个参照对象，再说明前面的事物或动作和这个参照对象有什么关系。这样的小词叫介词。介词后面的名词或代词叫介词宾语；介词和它后面的部分合在一起，叫介词短语。<#0.8#>
判断时做三件事：找到这个关系词；抓住它后面的参照对象；再问它交代的是位置、时间、方向、参与者，还是别的关系。先看关系，再看中文意思，介词就不会变成一堆零散翻译。

lessons.title: What prepositions are
examples: The game stopped because of the rain.
The cat came out of the box.

analyses.label: Complex prepositional phrase as reason adverbial

exampleNotes.body: after is the preposition; lunch is its object.
because of is a complex preposition taking a noun phrase.
out of plus the object the box forms a prepositional phrase.

rules: after is a one-word preposition and forms a phrase with lunch.
because of and in front of are multiword prepositions.
A preposition expresses a relation; together with its object it forms a prepositional phrase.

questions.correct: after is the preposition; lunch is its object.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: after is the preposition; lunch is its object.

questions.question: ___ the rain takes a noun phrase.
questions.correct: because of is a complex preposition taking a noun phrase.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: because of is a complex preposition taking a noun phrase.

questions.question: What is the whole unit “out of the box”?
questions.correct: out of plus the object the box forms a prepositional phrase.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: out of plus the object the box forms a prepositional phrase.

narration.text: 约好午饭后见面，页面第一句是。<#0.4#>We met after lunch。<#0.8#>after 只有一个词，后面带 lunch，把见面安排在午饭之后。这种单个词直接建立关系的，叫简单介词。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The game stopped because of the rain。<#0.8#>这里建立原因关系的部分由两个词组成，却要合起来理解，不能只拿其中一个词分析。这类整体叫复合介词。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The cat came out of the box。<#0.8#>这里的关系词组也要整体看，它从盒子内部出发，交代猫离开的起点。页面三组关系结构都是介词连同后面对象组成的介词短语。<#0.8#>本节只解决“介词长什么样”：它可能是一个词，也可能是几个词组成的固定整体。判断时先找后面的参照对象，再向前确认究竟由一个词还是一组词共同建立关系；一组词若缺一部分就失去原意，就按整体识别。

lessons.title: Prepositions and their objects

exampleNotes.body: Use object form me after a preposition.
A noun phrase can be the object.

A preposition can take a noun phrase.
A verb after a preposition uses the -ing form.

questions.correct: Use object form me after a preposition.

narration.text: 座位在谁旁边，要把那个人说出来。<#0.4#>She sat beside me。<#0.8#>beside 先给出“旁边”的关系，me 再提供参照对象。这里不能用 I，因为代词放在介词后面，要用宾格 me。这个被介词带出的对象，叫介词宾语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>We talked about the plan。<#0.8#>about 说明谈话围绕什么，the plan 是完整的名词短语，负责把话题补清楚。介词如果没有后面的对象，关系通常就悬空了。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Before leaving, he called me。<#0.8#>before 后面想放“离开”这个动作时，不能直接放动词原形，而要用 leaving。这里 leaving 把动作当成一件事情，作为介词宾语。<#0.8#>本节重点不是再认介词，而是看介词后面能放什么。操作时先圈介词，再圈紧跟它的完整对象：代词要用宾格，名词要把整个短语圈全，动作放在介词后通常用 ing 形式。

lessons.title: Prepositions, conjunctions and particles
lessons.meta: Identify the following unit and syntactic role
examples: I look forward to meeting you.

exampleNotes.body: before is followed by the noun phrase dinner, so it is a preposition here.
Here to is a preposition and takes the gerund meeting.
up forms a phrasal verb with look; the word is the object of look up.

rules: before is a preposition before a noun phrase and a conjunction before a clause.
Prepositional to takes a noun or gerund; infinitival to takes a base verb.
Items such as up in a phrasal verb are particles; a preposition introduces its own object and relation.

questions.question: What is before in “before we ate”?
questions.correct: we ate is a clause, so before is a conjunction.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: we ate is a clause, so before is a conjunction.

questions.question: look forward to ___ you
questions.correct: Here to is a preposition and takes the gerund meeting.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Here to is a preposition and takes the gerund meeting.

questions.question: What is up in “look up the word”?
questions.correct: up forms a phrasal verb with look; the word is the object of look up.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: up forms a phrasal verb with look; the word is the object of look up.

narration.text: 同一个小词，换了后面的结构，工作可能完全不同。先看。<#0.4#>Before dinner, we walked。<#0.8#>before 后面直接带名词 dinner，合起来说明 walked 发生的时间，所以这里 before 是介词。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>I look forward to meeting you。<#0.8#>这里 to 后面接 meeting，表示期待指向的事情。to 属于 look forward to 这个关系结构中的介词，所以后面的动作要用 ing 形式，不能因为看到 to 就自动判断为不定式标记。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Please look up the word。<#0.8#>up 后面没有自己的介词宾语，它和 look 合起来表达“查找”，the word 是整个 look up 的宾语。这里 up 叫小品词。<#0.8#>判断边界时，先看小词后面有没有名词、代词或 ing 形式作为自己的对象；有对象并建立关系，通常按介词分析。若后面接完整分句，可能是连词；若和动词合成整体、没有自己的对象，就考虑小品词。

Use on for days and dates.
Use in for months, seasons, years and longer periods.
from...to expresses a start-to-end range.
since marks a starting point extending to the present.
for expresses a duration.

narration.text: 安排日程时，先看时间像一个点、一页日历，还是一段较长的范围。<#0.4#>The class starts at six。<#0.8#>six 是钟表上的具体时刻，所以用 at。<#0.5#>We meet on Monday。<#0.8#>Monday 是日历上的一天，所以用 on。<#0.5#>Birds return in spring。<#0.8#>spring 是包住许多天的一段季节，所以用 in。<#0.7#>接着看起止。<#0.4#>The library is open from nine to five。<#0.8#>from 标出起点，to 标出终点，两边合起来画出开放的时间范围。<#0.7#>She has lived here since 2020 里，since 把 2020 当成起点，并把状态拉到现在；We waited for two hours 里，for 不说从哪天开始，只量出持续了两小时。<#0.8#>本节把基础时间关系放进一张图。判断时先问：是具体时刻、某一天，还是较长时段；再看句子要的是起点、终点还是持续长度。点钟选 at，日期和星期选 on，月份季节年份等选 in；起止、起点和时长再分别检查 from to、since、for。

lessons.title: Endpoints, periods and deadlines
examples: Please finish the work by Friday.
No phones rang during the meeting.

exampleNotes.body: Use by for a deadline.
Use until for continuation to an endpoint.
during places rang within the period of the meeting: no phones rang in that period.

rules: by means no later than a time and marks a deadline.
until marks how long an action or state continues.
during takes an event or period noun; within means before a limited period ends.

questions.question: Finish it no later than Friday: finish it ___ Friday
questions.correct: Use by for a deadline.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use by for a deadline.

questions.question: We continued waiting up to noon: waited ___ noon
questions.correct: Use until for continuation to an endpoint.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use until for continuation to an endpoint.

questions.correct: Use within for a limited period.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use within for a limited period.

narration.text: 任务写着周五前交，重点不是一直做到周五，而是最晚不能超过周五。<#0.4#>Please finish the work by Friday。<#0.8#>by 给出截止线，周五之前任何时候完成都可以。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>We waited until noon。<#0.8#>until 让 waited 这个动作持续到中午，中午是等待停止的终点。by 关心“最迟何时完成”，until 关心“状态一直延续到何时”。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>No phones rang during the meeting。<#0.8#>during 把 rang 放进 meeting 这段期间，说明整场会议之中没有电话响；它只标期间，不直接说明动作持续多久。within 则常表示必须落在给定期限内部。<#0.8#>判断时先看动作类型：是要在某条线之前完成，用 by；是一直维持到终点，用 until；是说某事件发生在一段活动中，用 during；是限定在多长时间以内，用 within。先画时间线，再选词。

lessons.title: Common time contrasts
lessons.meta: in · after · on time · in time
examples: The train will leave in ten minutes.
We arrived in time for the bus.

analyses.label: Time after a past reference point

exampleNotes.body: Use in for a future point measured from now.
Use after when measuring from a stated reference point.
Use in time for early enough.

rules: in + duration refers to a future point measured from now.
after + duration is normally measured from a past or contextual reference point.
on time means punctually; in time means early enough.

questions.question: The train leaves ten minutes from now: leave ___ ten minutes
questions.correct: Use in for a future point measured from now.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use in for a future point measured from now.

questions.question: He returned two days after leaving: returned ___ two days
questions.correct: Use after when measuring from a stated reference point.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use after when measuring from a stated reference point.

questions.question: We arrived early enough for the bus: arrived ___ for the bus
questions.correct: Use in time for early enough.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use in time for early enough.

narration.text: 两天以后和两天之内，中文听着接近，英语看的时间起点不同。先看。<#0.4#>The train will leave in ten minutes。<#0.8#>in ten minutes 从“现在”往后数十分钟，表示十分钟后列车将离开，常和将来情境连用。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>He returned after two days。<#0.8#>after two days 是从语境中已经确定的某个事件起，再过两天返回。它不一定以说话此刻为起点。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>We arrived in time for the bus。<#0.8#>in time 表示赶在错过之前到达，虽然可能不早，但还来得及；on time 则强调正好按计划时间，不迟到。<#0.8#>判断时先找计时起点：从现在往后多久，多考虑 in；从前文事件之后多久，用 after。再看重点是“准点”还是“还来得及”：按时刻表是 on time，赶上最后机会是 in time。

lessons.title: Prepositions of place

A picture hangs above the desk.

exampleNotes.body: Use at for a point.
Use in for an interior.
above means higher, not touching a surface.
Use on for surface contact.
below means lower than.
over commonly means directly above.

rules: at marks a place as a point.
in marks an interior.
on marks contact with a surface.
above/below mean higher or lower without requiring direct alignment.
over/under commonly mean directly above or below.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use at for a point.

questions.question: Inside the box: ___ the box
questions.correct: Use in for an interior.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use in for an interior.

questions.correct: above means higher, not touching a surface.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: above means higher, not touching a surface.

questions.correct: Use on for surface contact.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use on for surface contact.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: below means lower than.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: over commonly means directly above.

narration.text: 找东西时，先决定把地点看成一个点、一个内部空间，还是一个接触面。<#0.4#>Tom waited at the gate。<#0.8#>at 把 gate 当作等待发生的点位。<#0.5#>The keys are in the box。<#0.8#>in 强调钥匙在盒子内部。<#0.7#>A picture hangs above the desk 里，above 只说明画比桌子高，不要求正对；The cup is on the table 里，on 还表示杯子接触桌面。<#0.7#>The valley lies below the village 中，below 表示山谷位置更低；A lamp hangs over the table 中，over 常让人看到灯在桌子上方覆盖或正对的画面。相应地，under 常用于正下方。<#0.8#>本节解决静态位置的基础视角。判断时先问：参照物被当成点、内部还是表面；再比较高低位置是否要求正对或覆盖。点位用 at，内部用 in，接触面用 on；单纯高低看 above、below，正上正下或覆盖关系再考虑 over、under。

examples: The bank is between the school and the park.

analyses.text: between the school and the park.
analyses.label: Place adverbial between two points

exampleNotes.body: Use between for two distinct places.
Use among within a group.
Use beside for next to.

rules: between relates two or clearly separate individual items.
among means within a group viewed collectively.
beside means next to; besides means in addition to.

questions.correct: Use between for two distinct places.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use between for two distinct places.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use among within a group.

narration.text: 描述位置时，“在中间”和“在旁边”最容易被中文带偏。先看。<#0.4#>The bank is between the school and the park。<#0.8#>学校和公园是两个清楚分开的参照，银行位于二者之间，所以用 between。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She stood among the crowd。<#0.8#>crowd 是一群围绕她的人，重点是处在群体之中，而不是精确夹在两个对象之间，所以用 among。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Ben sat beside me。<#0.8#>beside 只表示 Ben 坐在我旁边。besides 多了 s 时，常表示“除……之外还包括”，不是空间上的旁边。<#0.8#>判断时先数参照关系：两个或几个分别明确列出的对象之间，用 between；处在未逐个列出的群体之中，用 among。再分清 beside 和 besides：一个说位置相邻，一个说范围追加。不要只凭中文都能译成“在……中”或“除外”来选。

lessons.title: Direction and movement
examples: The cat jumped onto the table.
The train went through the tunnel.

exampleNotes.body: into marks movement inward.
onto marks movement to a surface.
across means from one side to the other.
through marks movement within an interior.

rules: in/on mark static position; into/onto mark movement to a position.
through marks movement within an enclosed space.
across marks movement from one side of a surface or area to another.

questions.correct: into marks movement inward.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: into marks movement inward.

questions.question: Jump to the surface: jump ___ the table
questions.correct: onto marks movement to a surface.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: onto marks movement to a surface.

questions.question: Run from one side of the road to the other
questions.correct: across means from one side to the other.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: across means from one side to the other.

questions.question: Move within the tunnel from end to end
questions.correct: through marks movement within an interior.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: through marks movement within an interior.

narration.text: 位置课回答“在哪里”，这一课回答“从哪里动到哪里”。<#0.4#>She walked into the room。<#0.8#>into 把走路的终点放到房间内部，既有方向，也有进入。<#0.5#>The cat jumped onto the table。<#0.8#>onto 表示猫跳动后到达桌面，并与表面接触。单说 in 或 on，通常只描写静态位置。<#0.7#>We ran across the road 中，across 画的是从道路一边横到另一边；The train went through the tunnel 中，through 画的是进入隧道内部，再从内部穿过。<#0.8#>to 只指向目标，不一定说明已经进入内部或落到表面；into 和 onto 把终点关系说得更具体。<#0.7#>判断运动介词，先找动作轨迹和终点：进入内部选 into，到达表面选 onto；横过一个表面或区域选 across，穿过有内部的空间选 through。最后检查句子是在说动态到达，还是已经处于 in、on 表示的位置。

lessons.title: Movement paths
examples: The hikers went through the forest.

exampleNotes.body: Use along for following a route.
Use past for movement beyond a point.
Use through for movement within an interior.

rules: along marks movement following a line or route.
past marks movement beyond a person or place.
across crosses a surface or area; through passes inside an enclosed space.

questions.correct: Use along for following a route.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use along for following a route.

questions.question: Run beyond the library: run ___ the library

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use past for movement beyond a point.

narration.text: 走路导航不仅要说终点，还要说一路怎样经过。<#0.4#>We walked along the river。<#0.8#>along 把路线贴着河流延伸，重点是沿着同一方向前进，不要求跨到河对岸。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She ran past the library。<#0.8#>past 把图书馆当成路上的参照点，她从它旁边经过并继续向前，重点是“超过、经过”这个点。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The hikers went through the forest。<#0.8#>through 表示徒步者进入森林内部，并沿内部路径穿行。across 则更强调从一个区域的一边到另一边。<#0.8#>判断路径时先画一条线：路线顺着某个线状参照延伸，用 along；越过路边的一个点，用 past；进入并穿行于空间内部，用 through；若重点是横跨表面或区域，再考虑 across。每个词回答的是轨迹形状，不只是“经过”的中文翻译。

lessons.title: Sources and separation
examples: The bird flew out of the cage.
The cup fell off the table.

exampleNotes.body: Use from for origin.
Use out of for movement from an interior.
Use off for movement away from a surface.

rules: from marks a source, origin or starting point.
out of marks movement from inside to outside.
off marks movement away from a surface.

questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use from for origin.

questions.question: The bird flew from inside the cage to outside.
questions.correct: Use out of for movement from an interior.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use out of for movement from an interior.

questions.question: The cup fell away from the table surface.
questions.correct: Use off for movement away from a surface.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use off for movement away from a surface.

narration.text: 运动不只看去向，也能回头看从哪里出发、从哪里脱离。<#0.4#>This train comes from Beijing。<#0.8#>from 把 Beijing 标成列车来源或起点，但不额外说明它原来在什么容器里。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The bird flew out of the cage。<#0.8#>out of 明确画出鸟原来在笼子内部，飞行后离开内部空间。它比单独的 from 多了“从里面出来”的画面。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The cup fell off the table。<#0.8#>off 说明杯子原来与桌面有接触，掉落后脱离这个表面。<#0.8#>判断时先问起点是什么关系：只交代来源或出发点，用 from；原来在内部、现在离开内部，用 out of；原来接触表面、现在脱离表面，用 off。把动作前后的两个位置都画出来，就不会把三个词都机械翻成“从”。

lessons.title: Means, instrument and agent
examples: She cut the paper with scissors.
The novel was written by Orwell.

exampleNotes.body: Use by for transport.
Use with for an instrument.
Use by for the agent.

rules: by + transport expresses the means of travel.
with + an instrument identifies the tool used.
In a passive clause, by introduces the agent.

questions.correct: Use by for transport.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use by for transport.

questions.question: Using scissors: ___ scissors
questions.correct: Use with for an instrument.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use with for an instrument.

questions.question: Painted ___ Monet
questions.correct: Use by for the agent.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use by for the agent.

narration.text: 同样译成“用”或“由”，英语会区分交通方式、手里的工具和动作执行者。<#0.4#>We travelled by train。<#0.8#>by train 把 train 当成出行方式，不是在强调某一列具体火车内部。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She cut the paper with scissors。<#0.8#>scissors 是她实际拿来剪纸的工具，所以用 with。这里动作执行者是 She，工具是 scissors，两者不能混。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The novel was written by Orwell。<#0.8#>句子把 novel 放在主语位置，was written 是被动结构，by Orwell 再补出写作动作由谁完成。这个 Orwell 叫施事，也就是动作执行者。<#0.8#>判断时先问后面的名词扮演什么角色：交通工具作为方式，用 by；手里使用的具体器具，用 with；被动句中补出谁做了动作，也用 by。不要只看中文都有一个“用”字。

lessons.title: Medium, language and presentation

exampleNotes.body: Use by email for the means of transmission.
Use on with the medium TV.
Use in with a language.

rules: by can mark a means of transmission, as in by email.
on is common with media such as TV, radio, the phone and online platforms.
in can mark language, colour, ink or form of presentation.

questions.question: Send it using email: send it ___ email
questions.correct: Use by email for the means of transmission.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use by email for the means of transmission.

questions.question: The match is broadcast ___ TV.
questions.correct: Use on with the medium TV.
questions.wrong: Check the rule: Use on with the medium TV.

questions.question: Answer using English: answer ___ English

narration.text: 发送消息、观看比赛、选择回答语言，都在说“通过什么呈现”，但关系不完全一样。<#0.4#>Please send it by email。<#0.8#>email 在这里是传递信息的渠道，by 强调通过这种方式发送。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The match is on TV。<#0.8#>on TV 表示比赛出现在电视这个传播平台上，重点是内容在哪个平台播出。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>She answered in English。<#0.8#>in English 说明回答采用的语言或表达形式，不是交通方式，也不是平台。<#0.8#>本节与上一课的工具关系相邻，但它专门区分媒介、平台和语言。判断时问三个问题：是在说信息通过什么渠道送出，内容在哪个平台呈现，还是用哪种语言或形式表达？渠道方式常用 by，平台常用 on，语言和表达形式常用 in。

rules: because of takes a noun phrase and expresses reason.
because takes a complete clause and expresses reason.
for + a noun or gerund can express use or purpose.
despite takes a noun or gerund and marks concession.
in spite of takes a noun or gerund and marks concession.

narration.text: 比赛为什么停、工具拿来做什么、天气虽冷还是否继续，是三种不同逻辑。<#0.4#>The match stopped because of the rain。<#0.8#>because of 后面带名词 the rain，把雨作为停止的原因。<#0.5#>This tool is for cutting glass。<#0.8#>for cutting glass 不说已经发生的动作，而是说明工具的用途。<#0.7#>Despite the cold, they continued 里，despite 承认寒冷这个阻碍，但主句结果仍然继续，这叫让步关系。<#0.7#>再对比。<#0.4#>We stayed home because it rained。<#0.8#>because 后面是 it rained 这个完整分句；because of 后面则是名词短语。最后看 In spite of being tired, she continued，in spite of 和 despite 一样建立让步，但它是三个词组成的整体，后面用 being tired。<#0.8#>判断时先分逻辑：解释原因、说明用途，还是承认阻碍仍有结果；再看后面接名词短语、ing 形式还是完整分句。原因短语用 because of，完整原因句用 because；用途看 for；让步看 despite 或 in spite of。

exampleNotes.body: The wood remains recognizable in the table, so made of identifies the visible material.
Use as for an actual role.
Use except to exclude Tom.

rules: made of keeps the material recognizable; made from suggests transformation.
like means similar to; as marks an actual role, identity or use.
except excludes; besides adds another included item.

narration.text: 看一张木桌，木头的样子仍然看得出来。<#0.4#>The table is made of wood。<#0.8#>of 把成品和仍可辨认的材料连起来，说明桌子的构成。若原料加工后已经看不出原样，通常会用另一种来源关系表达，本节先抓住“材料仍可辨认”这条线。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She works as a doctor。<#0.8#>as a doctor 说明她实际以医生的身份工作，不是在说她像医生。like 更偏向相似，as 更强调真实身份或承担的角色。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Everyone came except Tom。<#0.8#>except 把 Tom 从 everyone 所包含的范围中排除，意思是其他人都来了。besides 则常把对象继续加进范围，方向相反。<#0.8#>判断时先找本节的三类关系：成品由什么材料构成，某人以什么身份行动，某对象是被排除还是被追加。材料看构成关系，身份区分 as 与相似的 like，范围区分排除的 except 与追加的 besides。

It states where the children played.
with introduces the instrument key.

rules: A prepositional phrase functions as a time adverbial when it locates the action in time.
A prepositional phrase functions as a place adverbial when it locates the action in space.
A prepositional phrase can also express manner, instrument, reason, purpose, condition or concession.

narration.text: 同一个动作说清以后，还可以补上什么时候、在哪里、用什么方式发生。<#0.4#>We will meet after class。<#0.8#>主干 We will meet 已经说明谁要见面，after class 只给 meet 加上时间，这整个介词短语叫时间状语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The children played in the garden。<#0.8#>in the garden 回答“在哪里玩”，修饰的是动作 played，所以是地点状语，不是 children 的种类。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>She opened the box with a key。<#0.8#>with a key 回答“用什么打开”，给动作增加工具关系，属于工具状语。<#0.8#>本节解决介词短语怎样挂到动作上。判断时先暂时拿掉介词短语，看句子主干是否仍成立；再问它是在补时间、地点、工具、原因还是方式。若它主要回答动作何时、何地、怎样发生，整体就按状语分析。

narration.text: 人群里要认出戴红帽子的男孩，英语先说男孩，再把特征放在后面。<#0.4#>The boy with a red cap is my brother。<#0.8#>with a red cap 紧跟 boy，帮助确定是哪一个男孩，所以整个短语修饰名词 boy，叫后置定语。中文通常把它移到名词前理解。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The books on the desk are mine。<#0.8#>on the desk 贴着 books，回答“哪些书”，不是在说明 are 发生在哪里。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Students from Class Two won。<#0.8#>from Class Two 限定 Students 的来源，确定获胜的是二班学生。<#0.8#>判断时先看介词短语是否紧跟名词，再问它在回答“哪一个、哪一些、什么样的”。若删掉后名词范围变宽，它通常是后置定语；若主要回答动作在哪里发生，则是地点状语。最后翻成中文时可把这段说明前移，但英语结构仍在名词后。

worked is an action predicate; the phrase adds place.

rules: A prepositional phrase can be predicative when it follows a linking verb and describes the subject.
A predicative prepositional phrase can express an abstract state, not only location.
To distinguish predicative from adverbial, check whether the preceding verb is linking or an action verb.

narration.text: 钥匙在哪里，句子可以直接用一段位置关系来回答。<#0.4#>The keys are on the desk。<#0.8#>are 像一座桥，on the desk 放在桥后说明主语 keys 所处的位置。整个介词短语在这里叫表语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The child is in danger。<#0.8#>in danger 不是真实空间内部，而是说明孩子处于危险状态；它仍通过 is 描写主语，所以也是表语。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>She worked in the library。<#0.8#>这里 worked 本身已经是完整动作，in the library 只补充工作地点，属于地点状语，不是表语。<#0.8#>判断时先看介词短语前面的动词：如果是 be 等系动词，短语直接说明主语在哪里或处于什么状态，按表语分析；如果前面是 worked 这类实义动作，短语只回答动作发生地点，通常是状语。不能只因位置在句尾就下结论。

rules: In listen to, to directs attention toward the object of listening.
In interested in, in places the interest within a field or area.
In answer to, to makes the answer point to and correspond to the question.
to commonly points an action or entity toward a target; in commonly places it within a field or area.
Relational meaning explains the choice, while usage conventions still need to be learned with the head word.

narration.text: 介词选择不是随便跟在词后，也不只是死背。先看。<#0.4#>She listens to music。<#0.8#>to 把听的注意方向引向 music，补清 listens 的目标。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>He is interested in science。<#0.8#>in 把兴趣放进 science 这个领域，说明兴趣所在的范围。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The answer to the question is clear。<#0.8#>to the question 放在 answer 后，让答案指向并对应那个问题。中文会把它前移理解，但英语把关系放在中心名词后。<#0.8#>本节开始研究中心词为什么选择某个介词：to 常有指向目标的感觉，in 常有处在领域或范围中的感觉。判断时先找中心词是动词、形容词还是名词，再问它要把关系指向目标、放入范围，还是建立对应；用关系帮助理解后，仍要把中心词和介词作为真实组合核对记忆。

narration.text: 谈话围绕旅行、讲座聚焦气候变化、女孩带着眼镜，这三句都在名词或动作旁补信息，却建立不同关系。<#0.4#>We talked about the trip。<#0.8#>about the trip 说明谈话围绕什么话题，修补的是 talked 的内容范围。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>A lecture on climate change begins now。<#0.8#>on climate change 紧跟 lecture，告诉我们讲座的专题，语气通常比普通谈话的 about 更聚焦、正式。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The girl with glasses is Amy。<#0.8#>with glasses 不是谈话内容，而是给 girl 增加外在特征，帮助听者认出是哪位女孩。<#0.8#>判断时先问短语靠着谁、在补什么：围绕动作的谈论内容常用 about；讲座、文章等聚焦的专题可用 on；给人物或事物附加“带有什么”的特征，用 with。不要因为中文都能出现“关于、有”就混选。

The need for change is clear.

exampleNotes.body: depend selects on as its complement.
proud takes of.

exampleNotes.detail: reason commonly takes for when naming what it explains.

rules: Some verbs require a selected prepositional complement, as in depend on.
Adjectives can select prepositional complements, as in proud of.
Nouns can take complements that specify their content, as in need for and reason for.

narration.text: 有些词说到一半，会让人自然追问“依靠什么、为哪件事骄傲、对什么的需要”。介词短语负责把这种未完成的关系补齐。<#0.4#>Success depends on effort。<#0.8#>depends 会追问依靠什么，on effort 是动词需要的补足成分。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>She is proud of her work。<#0.8#>proud 只说“骄傲”还没有交代对象，of her work 补清骄傲所针对的事情，所以补足形容词 proud。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The need for change is clear。<#0.8#>for change 紧跟名词 need，说明是什么方面的需要，补足名词意义。<#0.8#>本节与普通状语不同：状语多是可选背景，补足成分由前面的中心词强烈要求。判断时先找介词短语前的动词、形容词或名词，再问去掉短语后是否留下“对谁、关于什么、依靠什么”的明显空缺；有空缺，就按相应中心词的补足成分分析。

narration.text: 同一个 agree，后面的介词一换，谈的对象类型也会变化。<#0.4#>I agree with you。<#0.8#>with 把我和 you 放进同一意见关系，表示我赞同你这个人表达的看法。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>We agreed on the date。<#0.8#>on the date 把 date 当成双方讨论后共同确定的事项，重点是就日期达成一致。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>They agreed to the plan。<#0.8#>to the plan 表示他们把同意指向这个方案，接受方案本身。<#0.8#>本节不是再背三个搭配，而是观察介词怎样改变 agree 后的关系：with 常连意见一致的人，on 常连协商确定的事项，to 常连被接受的建议或方案。判断时先辨认后面是人、共同议定事项，还是需要接受的内容；再选介词，并把整个关系放回语境检查。

narration.text: 介词后面不一定只有一个短名词，有时会带一整块信息。<#0.4#>We talked about what he said。<#0.8#>about 后面的 what he said 整体回答“谈论什么”，所以整块内容作为介词宾语，内部仍有自己的结构。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>Who are you talking to？<#0.8#>to 的对象是 Who，但疑问词被移到句首，介词留在句尾。这种位置变化不代表 to 没有对象。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>The person I spoke to is here。<#0.8#>I spoke to 说明 The person，to 的对象由前面的 person 补回理解，介词同样可以留在从句末尾。<#0.8#>判断复杂介词宾语时，先找介词建立的关系，再追问对象是否被展开成 wh 从句，或因疑问、定语从句移到前面。把移走的对象在心里放回介词后，关系能闭合，就不要把句尾介词误判成多余。

narration.text: 同一个地点短语放在不同位置，会挂到不同对象上。先看。<#0.4#>The students in the library are reading。<#0.8#>句中的地点关系紧跟 students，回答“哪些学生”，所以它修饰名词，是后置定语。<#0.7#>再看。<#0.4#>The students are reading in the library。<#0.8#>这次句子先出现完整动作 are reading，后面的地点关系回答“在哪里读”，所以它修饰动作，是地点状语。<#0.7#>第三句是。<#0.4#>Who are you speaking to？<#0.8#>to 虽在句尾，仍和句首 Who 建立说话对象关系，Who 是被移到前面的介词宾语。<#0.8#>综合判断按三步走：先找介词和它真正的对象，确定位置、时间或其他关系；再划清介词短语边界；最后看整个短语贴着名词作后置定语，挂在动作上作状语，还是补足中心词。若对象被前移，再把它放回去验证关系。
